es.summary: Oseltamivir es un inhibidor de la neuraminidasa usado para tratar y prevenir la influenza. Debe iniciarse dentro de las 48 h del inicio de síntomas.
key_points: Inhibidor de la neuraminidasa que impide la liberación de viriones.
Eficaz contra influenza A y B si se administra temprano.
Dosis oral; la forma líquida se usa en niños y pacientes con disfagia.
Efectos adversos comunes: náuseas, vómitos y dolor abdominal.
Precaución en pacientes con insuficiencia renal; ajustar la dosis.
No sustituye la vacunación anual contra la influenza.

mechanism: Bloquea la enzima neuraminidasa viral, evitando la liberación de nuevas partículas virales.
Reduce la propagación del virus en el epitelio respiratorio.
Disminuye la carga viral y acorta la duración de los síntomas.
indications: Tratamiento de influenza no complicada en pacientes ≥1 año.
Profilaxis postexposición en contactos cercanos sin inmunidad.
Uso en brotes institucionales para reducir transmisión.
contraindications: Hipersensibilidad conocida al oseltamivir o a sus excipientes.
Pacientes con insuficiencia renal grave sin ajuste de dosis.
interactions: Puede aumentar los niveles de warfarina; monitorizar INR.
Los inhibidores de la bomba de protones pueden retrasar la absorción.
No se ha demostrado interacción significativa con vacunas contra la influenza.
nursing_care: Verificar que el paciente haya iniciado el tratamiento ≤48 h del inicio de síntomas.
Evaluar función renal (creatinina) antes de iniciar; ajustar dosis si eGFR <30 mL/min.
Administrar con alimentos o leche para minimizar náuseas.
Monitorear signos de sangrado gastrointestinal si usa AINEs concomitantes.
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si aparecen reacciones cutáneas graves.
patient_teaching: Tomar el medicamento exactamente como se indica, sin omitir dosis.
Completar el curso completo aun si los síntomas mejoran.
Tomar con alimentos o leche para reducir malestar estomacal.
Informar al profesional de salud si aparecen erupciones, fiebre alta o dificultad respiratoria.
Mantener la vacunación anual contra la influenza.

outcomes: Control de la infección: paciente sin signos de infección en 48 h.
Adherencia al tratamiento: paciente completa 100 % de las dosis prescritas.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de iniciar el antiviral dentro de 48 h.
interventions.rationale: El beneficio clínico disminuye significativamente después de ese periodo.

interventions.action: Verificar la función renal y ajustar la dosis según protocolos.
interventions.rationale: Previene acumulación y toxicidad del fármaco.

interventions.action: Reforzar la adherencia mediante recordatorios y registro de dosis.
interventions.rationale: Reduce el riesgo de falla terapéutica y resistencia viral.

interventions.action: Monitorear signos de efectos adversos gastrointestinales y reportar al médico.
interventions.rationale: Permite intervención temprana y evita complicaciones.

interventions.action: Promover la vacunación anual contra la influenza.
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la probabilidad de infección y necesidad de antivirales.

en.summary: Oseltamivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor used to treat and prevent influenza. It should be started within 48 h of symptom onset.
key_points: Neuraminidase inhibitor that blocks virion release.
Effective against influenza A and B when given early.
Oral dosing; liquid form used in children and patients with dysphagia.
Common adverse effects: nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain.
Caution in patients with renal impairment; dose adjustment required.
Does not replace annual influenza vaccination.

mechanism: Blocks viral neuraminidase enzyme, preventing release of new viral particles.
Reduces viral spread in the respiratory epithelium.
Decreases viral load and shortens symptom duration.
indications: Treatment of uncomplicated influenza in patients ≥1 year.
Post‑exposure prophylaxis for close contacts without immunity.
Use in institutional outbreaks to reduce transmission.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to oseltamivir or its excipients.
Severe renal failure without dose adjustment.
interactions: May increase warfarin levels; monitor INR.
No significant interaction with influenza vaccines has been demonstrated.
nursing_care: Verify that the patient started treatment ≤48 h from symptom onset.
Assess renal function (creatinine) before initiation; adjust dose if eGFR <30 mL/min.
Administer with food or milk to minimize nausea.
Monitor for GI bleeding signs if concurrent NSAIDs are used.
Hold dose and notify the physician if severe skin reactions occur.
patient_teaching: Take the medication exactly as prescribed, do not skip doses.
Complete the full course even if symptoms improve.
Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset.
Inform the healthcare provider if rashes, high fever, or breathing difficulty occur.

outcomes: Infection control: patient without signs of infection within 48 h.
Treatment adherence: patient completes 100 % of prescribed doses.

interventions.action: Educate the patient on the importance of starting the antiviral within 48 h.
interventions.rationale: Clinical benefit decreases significantly after that period.

interventions.action: Verify renal function and adjust dose per protocol.
Reinforce adherence with reminders and dose logs.
interventions.rationale: Reduces risk of therapeutic failure and viral resistance.

interventions.action: Monitor for GI adverse effect signs and report to the physician.
interventions.rationale: Allows early intervention and prevents complications.
Reduces infection probability and antiviral need.

summary.0.quote: The primary class of drugs used to treat influenza infection includes the neuraminidase inhibitors oseltamivir, zanamivir, and peramivir.

summary.1.quote: Clients using the episodic method must be instructed to begin taking their therapy within 24 hours of symptom onset for the medication to be effective.

key_points.0.quote: Neuraminidase inhibitors work by inhibiting the enzyme neuraminidase, which is used to cleave mature copies of the virus from an infected cell to allow it to go infect other cells.

sections.mechanism.0.quote: Neuraminidase inhibitors work by inhibiting the enzyme neuraminidase, which is used to cleave mature copies of the virus from an infected cell to allow it to go infect other cells.

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: Most oral antibiotics can cause gastrointestinal discomfort, including nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.

sections.adverse_effects.1.quote: Adverse Effects Headache Skin rash Abdominal pain Diarrhea Dizziness QT interval prolongation Contraindications Hypersensitivity Pregnancy Coadministration with QT interval–prolonging drugs

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: Initiation of molnupiravir should occur within 5 days of symptom onset.

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: Alert their health care provider about any signs of allergic reactions, including throat swelling, severe itching, rash, or chest tightness.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Advise the client to take the entire prescribed course of the medication to ensure adequate treatment and to reduce the development of antibiotic drug resistance.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Take the entire course of antibiotics, even if they begin to feel better.

sections.patient_teaching.4.quote: Annual vaccination will not prevent all infections but may help reduce the symptoms that individuals experience, and it is critical for protecting people most at risk for complications, such as older adults and immunocompromised individuals.
